title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
statement:
An array of `n` **distinct** integers was originally sorted in ascending order and then rotated an unknown number of times. One rotation moves the first element to the end, so rotating `[1, 3, 6, 9]` once gives `[3, 6, 9, 1]`, twice gives `[6, 9, 1, 3]`, and so on. Rotating `n` times (or zero times) gives the original sorted array back.

Given the rotated array, print its smallest element.

Reading the input is linear, but your algorithm itself should run in `O(log n)` time: do not scan the whole array.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` distinct integers: the rotated array.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the minimum element of the array.
constraints: The array is a rotation of a strictly ascending array

examples.explanation: The sorted array `2 5 8 11 14 17` was rotated so that 11 comes first. The drop from 17 to 2 marks the rotation point, and 2 is the minimum.
The array is not rotated at all, so the minimum is the first element.
The original array was `-4 0 9`; after rotation the minimum -4 sits in the middle.

hints: The minimum is the only element whose predecessor (cyclically) is larger. Where can the 'drop' be relative to the middle element?
Compare `nums[mid]` with `nums[hi]`. If `nums[mid] > nums[hi]`, the minimum lies strictly to the right of `mid`; otherwise it is at `mid` or to its left.
Keep shrinking `[lo, hi]` with `hi = mid` (not `mid - 1`) in the second case, and stop when `lo == hi`.
